title: Open Bounty Schema — Token Profile
description: Describes a token a bounty can be paid in, and everything holding it unlocks for the shopper. Added in v0.3. A program with an unbounded and growing set of tokens must be able to add one without a schema release, so this schema validates the SHAPE of a profile and never enumerates known symbols.

symbol.description: The token's stable key. Validated by PATTERN, never by an enum — a token the issuer has not created yet must already be valid here, or adding one would require a schema release.

canonical_url.description: The token's identity. Store objects reference this and nothing else.

listed.description: Whether the issuer lists this token publicly. False means reachable by direct URL but absent from the roster — how a token that exists but has no published copy yet stays honest rather than hidden.

lifecycle.description: Where the token is in its life. An open vocabulary by design: an issuer may define its own stages, and a consumer must not assume this set. In the reference implementation, `live` is set only when the token actually launches and is the one value a member-facing surface may treat as real; a `paused` token is unlisted, stays reachable by URL, and every unlock beneath it reads as `planned`.

engine.description: The programme, cause or category this token belongs to. Null for a network-wide token that belongs to none.

earn.description: How the token is earned. Null while no member-facing sentence has been written — which is the honest state for a token that is not yet listed.

display.description: ONE human sentence, shown verbatim by agents. Capped to keep it a sentence rather than a pitch.

also_earned_by.description: Short phrases for non-purchase earning. Never a rate.

basis.description: What the ladder is measured against.

note.description: What this ladder does and does not do. Where a programme has a separate earning multiplier, this must say the ladder is not it — a ladder of thresholds with no such statement invites the reader to infer that holding multiplies earning.

rungs.description: The ladder, in order. ANY length: no minItems and no enum of rung names, because a ladder is per-token and overridable. A consumer must not assume a rung count, a set of names, or a set of thresholds.

label.description: The member-facing name of this rung. Derived by the issuer, not authored per row.

unlocks_summary.description: Counts by state, so an agent can tell at a glance whether anything is actually available without walking the array.

unlocks_url.description: The live unlocks feed. Authoritative over the embedded unlocks array.

state.description: planned: in design, and NEVER presentable as available. committed: a written commitment from the partner is on file, but it is not yet available. funded: money is behind it and it is available. This IS a closed enum, deliberately — unlike symbols and rungs, the three states are the load-bearing honesty guarantee of the whole object, and a programme inventing a fourth would break what an agent can rely on.

opens_at.description: Only where a date is genuinely known. Null is the honest default.

sponsor.description: Named ONLY where that partner granted attribution and the unlock has reached committed or funded. A planned unlock must never name a partner: doing so asserts a relationship that does not exist.
